subject: Support playbook / credits — counterparty review and redlines
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: tom.s@contracts.acme.com
Date: 2026-10-01T14:12:00Z
Subject: Draft support playbook & SLA questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending the draft support playbook earlier today. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the SLA section and have a few open items we'd like to clarify before we proceed to procurement:

- Uptime target: are you able to confirm if the platform SLA is 99.95% or 99.9%? The draft language we saw was inconsistent between the MSA and the Order Form.
- Service credits: the formula caps credits at a percentage of monthly fees; please confirm the cap and whether there's a cumulative cap per rolling 12-months.
- Response times: P1 defined as 1 hour in the Ops notes — can you confirm that the Engineering on-call will acknowledge within 1 hour and provide a remediation ETA within 2 hours?
- Maintenance windows: we request blackout periods for our peak events (Black Friday weekends). How are emergency maintenance events handled and how will we be notified?

We need this clarified by EOD Friday (2026-10-08) to align with our quarter-close procurement timeline.

Attached: Acme_SLA_Questions.xlsx (list of requested clarifications).

Regards,
Lena Park
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft support playbook & SLA questions

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short counterproposal and attached an updated SLA playbook (Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v3.pdf) with inline notes. High level:

- Uptime target: we propose 99.95% for "core inference endpoints" and 99.9% for experimental/preview models. This lets us guarantee production paths while giving flexibility for model rollouts.
- Service credits: tiered credits at 5%, 10%, 25% of monthly recurring charges by severity band; cumulative cap = 3x monthly recurring charges in any 12-month rolling period.
- P1 response: acknowledge within 30 minutes (automated paging + on-call), remediation ETA within 2 hours; P2 acknowledge within 4 hours.
- Maintenance: regular monthly maintenance windows (first Sunday 03:00–05:00 UTC). Emergency maintenance permitted for critical security or data integrity issues — we will notify via email + status.redwood.com and provide a post-mortem within 48 hours. We will accept scheduled blackout dates for recognized peak events if notified 90 days in advance.

If that looks acceptable to you, I suggest we lock these terms in the Order Form and iterate on the exact credit calculation with Legal. Next step: Marissa and I will map the mutual action plan; Laura will coordinate legal redlines.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v3.pdf (redline comments).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft support playbook & SLA questions

Team — quick negotiation play to share before we hand to Acme:

1) Push for 99.95 on core. We can accept 99.9 on preview models but make it explicit in Exhibit A which model IDs are preview.
2) Service credit cap: aim for 3x monthly (as Rachel suggested). If Legal pushes back, agree to 2x but only after they justify from an enterprise risk POV.
3) P1 response — 30 minutes acknowledgement is a commercial win; be ready to show our recent on-call paging metrics in the call.
4) Maintenance blackout/scheduling: offer a commercial concession — one guaranteed Black Friday weekend blackout per 12 months (we own the rest).

Action items: Marcus, collect the ops SLIs to back the 30 minute ack claim. Laura, prepare an Order Form redline with the credit calc expressed as percentage bands + an explicit exclusion list for scheduled maintenance 

I'll draft the mutual action plan and share a timeline to get to DocuSign by 2026-10-15.

- Marissa
Senior Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:40:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft support playbook & SLA questions — legal redlines

Team,

I've reviewed the draft and propose these concrete redlines to protect Redwood while keeping the deal moving:

- Service credit calculation: define credit buckets (<=99.5% = 25%, (99.5,99.8] = 10%, (99.8,99.95] = 5%). Cap = 3x MRC per 12-month rolling period.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (defined by a 48-hour notice window) and force majeure.
- Downtime measurement: use service-side metrics aggregated at the account level; include a 15-minute minimum incident duration to qualify.
- Liability: carve out unlimited liability; limit liability to total fees paid in prior 12 months, excluding willful misconduct.
- Data/export: require a 60-day export window on termination and a signed SOP for data deletion.

I'll prepare an Order Form redline (word doc) and highlight anything likely to attract counterparty pushback. Marcus — please attach the operational measurement doc you mentioned; it will help justify the 15-minute threshold.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Tom S. <tom.s@contracts.acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>, contracts@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft support playbook & SLA questions

Rachel — thanks. A couple items from our side:

- We can agree to differential uptime (core vs preview) but Acme's procurement prefers a single guaranteed number where possible. We'd accept 99.9% across the board if you can move the P1 acknowledgement to 1 hour instead of 30 minutes.
- Regarding credits, a rolling 12-month cap is fine but we need the cap expressed as a percentage of ARR rather than raw months of MRC.
- Procurement is on a tight calendar; we need an executed Order Form by 2026-10-14 to meet our vendor onboarding schedule. I will send a DocuSign link once our legal and procurement teams have your redlines.

Tom S.
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom S. <tom.s@contracts.acme.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft support playbook & SLA questions — proposed compromise and next steps

Tom / Lena — appreciate the fast turnaround. To keep momentum, here's a pragmatic compromise we can take to DocuSign:

- Uptime: 99.95% for core inference endpoints; 99.9% for preview models. We'll include a short definitions table in Exhibit A that pins specific model IDs to each bucket.
- P1 response: acknowledgement within 45 minutes; remediation ETA within 2 hours. We will share our on-call paging metrics during the redline call.
- Service credits: banded percentages as Laura proposed, cap expressed as the lesser of 3x monthly recurring charges or 1.5% of trailing 12 month ARR (this gives a workable proxy to Acme's ask).
- Maintenance: allow 1 Black Friday blackout per 12-month period if Acme provides 90-day notice. Emergency maintenance requires immediate notice and a 48-hour post-event report.

Attached: Redlines_acme_orderform.docx (redline vs your earlier counters). Proposed next steps:
1) Legal redline call (30 min) — Laura + Marcus + Acme legal — proposed slot 2026-10-05 10:00–10:30 PT.
2) Mutual action plan from Marissa — please circulate by EOD 2026-10-03.
3) DocuSign target: 2026-10-14.

If that timeline works, we will prepare the final Order Form and send to your contracting team.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redlines_acme_orderform.docx
